title: Casting the small-bias Fourier estimate
statement: Let $n,a,b,s$ be natural numbers with $0<n$, $0<a$, $2a\le b$, and $1\le s$, and consider the small-bias Fourier input with dimension $n$, bias numerator $a$, bias denominator $b$, and Fourier bound $s$. Let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube and let $U$ be a set of coordinates in the generator's output dimension. The rational empirical Fourier coefficient obtained from the generated samples labeled by $f$, when viewed as a real number, equals the real sample Fourier estimate of $f$ on $U$.
hypotheses_covered: Twice the bias numerator is at most the bias denominator: $2a\le b$
A sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
A subset $U$ of the output coordinates
